releases.notes: Updates from Diastema support: when your server is connected to Diastema, Diastema support can now install an update for you (usually overnight, at the install time in Settings → About), go back to an earlier version if an update causes trouble, and adjust your update settings. Settings → About shows anything scheduled and who installed the last update. As always, only updates signed by Diastema are installed, your data is backed up first, and the previous version is put back automatically if a new one doesn't start.

One address for everyone: the office's computers can now use your office's secure address too, like iPads and phones. Add each computer once (Settings → Devices; admins can make one code for several computers). Browsers use HTTP/2 through it, so each page loads over a single connection. The office-network address (http://SERVER:8080) becomes an advanced option in Settings → About: it always works on the server itself, and for other computers only while an admin has it on, for example while the internet is down. It stays on after this update until you turn it off, so nothing changes until you're ready. The Open Dental button can now open the secure address (Settings → About shows the path to use).

iPads, phones and computers are added once, then open Diastema at your office's secure address from anywhere, not just on the office's internet connection. Add one from Settings → Devices (scan the QR code with the device, or type the short code on it), or, on the office's internet connection, tap "Ask to add it" on the device and approve it from the banner after checking the number on its screen. Managers and admins can add and remove devices (Settings → Users & access). After this update, each iPad and phone that already uses the secure address needs to be added once. Everyone still signs in with their PIN; 10 wrong PINs in a row on one device remove it. Computers using the office-network address aren't affected.

iPads and phones connect more reliably. Diastema's connection to diastema.app now uses secure WebSockets, the standard that office firewalls and web filters already allow, and an iPad's or phone's first request no longer fails after the office has been quiet for a few minutes. Update the server soon: diastema.app now expects this kind of connection, so iPads and phones can't reach Diastema through it until the server is updated. Computers in the office aren't affected.

iPads and phones in the office: an admin can turn it on in Settings → About. Staff then open Diastema on an iPad or phone on the office Wi-Fi at your office's own address (shown there, with a QR code to scan), with a real certificate that this server holds and renews on its own. Everyone still signs in with their PIN. Computers in the office keep using Diastema exactly as before, even when the internet is down.

Off-site copies with Diastema: an admin can tick “Also keep an off-site copy with Diastema” on the Automatic backups card (Settings → Backup & restore; needs the Diastema connection). Each night's backup file, still locked with the recovery code, also goes to Diastema's off-site storage and is kept 14 days. A fresh install can restore from it on the setup page with a restore code from Diastema support.

Missed calls can now go through Diastema's own mailbox instead of the WordPress plugin: Settings → Phone calls → Switch to Diastema's mailbox, then paste the new webhook address into Mango. The WordPress mailbox is still emptied until you stop it, so no call is lost while you change Mango.

Connected to Diastema: an admin can connect this server in Settings → About with a one-time enrollment code from Diastema. Once connected it sends a short status every 15 minutes (versions, whether Open Dental answers, backups on or off), never patient data.
First-run setup now ends with an optional step to add the Diastema button to Open Dental (Skip for now to do it later in Settings → About). The Open Dental button steps also fit on phone screens.

Open Dental button: Settings → About → Open Dental button walks admins through adding a Diastema button to Open Dental's toolbar (values ready to copy, a button icon to download, and a check that it's set up). Clicking it opens the selected patient's Diastema page.

New: Settings > About > Go back to an earlier version (admins). Pick any earlier release that works with your data (0.5.0-beta.11 or newer; beta channel lists betas and stable, stable lists stable) with its release notes. Diastema backs up the database, installs it, and puts the current version back if the earlier one doesn't start. Overnight automatic updates are turned off so the version you left doesn't come right back.

New: Settings > Backup & restore (admins). Download backup makes one password-protected file with everything needed to bring Diastema back after a failed update, a reinstall or a move to a new server (users and PINs, follow-ups, tasks, history, settings, header image, the Open Dental connection and the phone-calls pairing). Restore from Settings, or from the setup page of a fresh install ('Restore from a backup file instead'): the file and password are checked first, Diastema restarts to finish, and the data it replaced is kept in backups\before-restore-...

Analytics: 'No comparison' option (no earlier periods loaded, no comparison table, faster). When comparing with 2 or more earlier periods, each tile shows a mini column chart of those periods and this one (hover a bar for its value). The comparison table is now folded under 'Show the numbers' (remembered).

Analytics: new 'Compare with' setting (previous 1 to 5 periods, remembered per device) and a comparison table with each key stat for this period, each earlier period, their average and the change. With more than one period the tiles compare against the average. Earlier periods now line up with the calendar (months with months, quarters with quarters, month-to-date with the same days of earlier months, a single day with the same weekday in earlier weeks).

Schedule: new Visual view (List / Visual switch, remembered per device). One column per shown operatory, always fitting the screen width, with each appointment as tall as its length, colored by kind of visit (checkup/cleaning, treatment, new patient, limited/emergency, or the color set in Open Dental). Blocks without room for details shrink to initials; tap one for its details and an Open patient button. Double-booked appointments sit side by side, today shows a red line at the current time, and - / + make the day taller or shorter.

Schedule on phones: each appointment is now a compact card (time, patient, age and badges, operatory and providers, procedures on one line, note) instead of one labelled line per field, so busy days need far less scrolling. Long appointment notes start cut to 2 lines on phones and 3 on desktop, with More / Less to see the whole note.
Fix: on the Schedule, the Today button's text no longer spills outside the button, and the date box no longer makes the page scroll sideways on phones.

New layout. Home is now the day Schedule: appointments with time, operatory, dentist/hygienist, procedures, confirmation and notes; previous/next day, Today and a date picker; show/hide operatories and hide completed (remembered on each device). Clicking a patient opens the new Patient page: follow-up status (with the full follow-up window), saved treatment plans (print as before), unscheduled treatment, appointments and tasks. Patient search is in the top bar on every page (press / to jump to it). 'Today' is renamed Follow-ups; the separate Treatment Plans page is gone.
X-ray audit: only exams with missed or removed X-rays are listed (the summary still counts every exam in the date range). The 'All exams' view is gone; the CSV download has the same problem exams.

Follow-ups: patients with anything other than a checkup or cleaning on the schedule (any code outside D0/D1, including office N-codes, or an appointment with no procedures) no longer come up as due on Today. Once that appointment has passed, if the treatment still isn't scheduled or done, the follow-up comes due again.

X-ray check: a comprehensive exam (D0150) visit with 4BW and 3 or more PAs now counts as an FMX, so it uses up the pano/FMX frequency (insurance may treat it as a full mouth series). Shown as the last pano/FMX where it applies. Settings > X-ray check can turn it off or change the exam codes and number of PAs.

Diastema 0.5.0. New since 0.4.0: X-ray check (bitewings, pano/FMX and extra PAs due at upcoming periodic exams by insurance frequency; one-click fix to add or remove X-rays on the appointment with undo and a running total; audit of past exams). Setup codes for connecting to Open Dental (or your own developer key), with keys encrypted on the server. Phone calls: missed calls from Mango Voice become tasks. Download support file. Fixes to the task window and updater.

New: Settings > About > Download support file (admins): version, settings, an Open Dental connection check, service logs and update history, with no keys, secrets, database contents or patient information (phone numbers and emails in logs are masked). Uninstaller now also removes the update task and downloaded updates, makes sure Diastema has stopped, and supports /DELETEDATA for silent uninstalls.
Fix: in the task window, the patient search list was cut off by the bottom of the window.

Phone calls: made for Mango Voice. Settings > Phone calls shows the full Mango webhook URL (with Mango's {CALLER_NUMBER}, {TIME_UTC} etc.). Each missed call becomes a task 'Missed phone call from (xxx) xxx-xxxx at 2:14 PM' for the person you choose, with caller ID and the line called in the notes. No patient matching. A repeated webhook for the same call is ignored.

New: Settings > Phone calls. Missed calls from the phone system (e.g. Mango Voice) become tasks: the phone system posts to the Diastema Connect mailbox on your website, where each call is encrypted for this office; Diastema collects every 30 seconds, matches the number to patients (caller first), and merges repeat calls into the open task. Off until paired and turned on.

Open Dental connection: offices can now connect with a single setup code from their Diastema provider, or (advanced) their own developer key. Saved keys are encrypted for the server (existing installs are encrypted 10 minutes after starting). About shows which kind of key is in use. If the data folder moves to another server, setup asks for the code again and keeps everything else.

X-ray audit: each past exam now shows the same reasoning as upcoming exams - the insurance frequency and how much was used, the last X-ray, when it was next allowed, and how many PAs would have fit (flagging when more were taken than fit).
X-ray audit: removed X-rays are listed only when insurance would have paid and no X-ray of that kind was done instead.
X-ray audit: removed X-rays that insurance wouldn't have paid for are no longer listed or counted.

X-ray check: new 'Audit past exams' tab (read-only). For completed periodic exams in a date range it shows what insurance would have paid for that wasn't done (bitewings, pano/FMX, PAs that would have fit), and X-rays removed from the appointment with who deleted them and when (flagging the day of the visit). CSV download. New permission 'Run the X-ray audit' (on for Managers).

X-ray check: running total of what the fix button has added (at each patient's fee schedule), how much of it is completed, and planned X-rays removed that insurance wouldn't pay. Managers and Admins can clear it to start over; the change history is kept.

X-ray check: the fix now adds the PAs that fit with bitewings (D0220 for the first, D0230 for each additional) on default teeth set in Settings (#8 and #24). Each appointment shows what the fix is worth at the patient's fee schedule, and the page shows the total in covered X-rays not yet scheduled.

X-ray check: one button per appointment adds the bitewings / pano that are due, or removes planned X-rays insurance won't cover and extra PAs. Undo for the last click. New access permission: Add or remove X-rays on appointments (on for Staff and Managers).

X-ray check: when bitewings are due or scheduled, shows how many extra PAs (up to 2) can be taken while bitewings + PAs stay under the FMX / pano fee at the patient's insurance fee schedule, and flags appointments with more PAs scheduled than fit. The comparison (lower of FMX and pano, FMX only, or pano only) is in Settings → X-ray check.

X-ray check now covers panos too: pano and FMX share one frequency, so the last pano or FMX decides when a new pano is allowed. Also flags X-rays allowed within 30 days after an exam (moving the appointment could get them covered) and plan frequencies that look mistyped in Open Dental.

New: X-ray check tab. Lists periodic exams in the next 4 weeks and whether bitewings are due under each patient's insurance BW frequency (from the last 4BW or FMX, including other-office X-rays in Insurance History). Flags bitewings already on an appointment that insurance won't cover yet.
Fixes: an update now finishes cleanly (the About page shows the result right away instead of 'Installing…'), and the page reloads only once after an update.
Test update: confirms updates install through Settings → About. No other changes.

First release with automatic updates. Settings → About now shows available updates, lets admins install them, and can install them overnight. Also includes the fix for the data-folder permissions during installation.
